asks: RecurrenceRule claims the full RRULE grammar, but the app implements a subset and rejects the rest. Narrow the spec, take a dependency, or leave the gap standing?
because: RecurrenceRule says "The full RRULE grammar applies, including BYDAY, COUNT and UNTIL." app/src/domain/recurrence.ts supports FREQ (DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, YEARLY), INTERVAL, BYDAY and UNTIL, and rejects COUNT, BYSETPOS, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH, BYWEEKNO, BYYEARDAY, WKST and the sub-daily frequencies. So the spec asserts something no implementation behind it delivers. COUNT is the sharpest case and the spec names it explicitly: honouring "repeat 5 times" needs a tally of occurrences so far, and Task carries no such attribute — it is not a parsing gap but a missing piece of the data model.

options.label: Narrow the spec to what is implemented
options.detail: Say exactly which RRULE parts are in scope, so the spec stops promising more than anything delivers. Cheapest, and honest — but it means a rule copied from a real calendar may be rejected, which is a surprising thing for a standard-shaped string to do.

proposal.summary: State the RRULE subset RecurrenceRule actually covers

ops.spec: A recurrence rule in RFC 5545 (iCalendar) RRULE form, such as "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2" or "FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=1MO". A defined subset of the grammar applies: FREQ (DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, YEARLY), INTERVAL, BYDAY — plain weekdays, or ordinals such as 1MO and -1FR for monthly rules — and UNTIL. A weekly rule without BYDAY repeats on the weekday it started from. Anything else, including COUNT, BYSETPOS, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH, BYWEEKNO, BYYEARDAY, WKST and the sub-daily frequencies, is rejected rather than approximated.

tests: "FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=5" is rejected, naming COUNT as unsupported
a weekly rule with no BYDAY repeats on the weekday it started from

options.label: Keep the full grammar and support it properly
options.detail: Leaves the spec as the standard says and makes the implementation meet it — in practice by taking an RRULE library rather than hand-rolling RFC 5545, which is large and subtle. Note this does not resolve COUNT on its own: bounded series still need somewhere to record how many occurrences have happened, so it likely pulls a second change behind it.

options.label: Add what COUNT needs, then decide the rest
options.detail: Treats the data-model gap as the real finding. A RecurringTask gains a count of completed occurrences, which is what makes COUNT expressible at all — and is arguably worth having anyway, since nothing currently records how many times a repeating Task has been done.

proposal.summary: Record how many occurrences of a RecurringTask have completed
tests: a new RecurringTask has completed no occurrences
completing a RecurringTask increments its occurrence count
reopening a RecurringTask does not decrement it

answer.chose: Narrow the spec to what is implemented
